summary: std::make_shared creates a shared_ptr with single allocation optimization. It constructs an object and wraps it in a std::shared_ptr, typically using a single memory allocation for both the object and its control block.
cpp17_notes: C++17 adds support for arrays with make_shared<T[]>() and make_shared_for_overwrite for default-initialized objects. The single-allocation optimization remains the primary advantage.
audio_thread_notes: std::make_shared MUST NOT be called from the audio thread. It allocates heap memory. Pre-allocate shared_ptr instances during initialization (prepareToPlay, constructor) and use atomics or lock-free structures to share them with the audio thread.
